input.instructions: Create a compact, accurate blueprint for an 8-to-12-minute educational lesson with exactly ten sequential teaching beats. Do not write full narration. Create exactly three measurable learning objectives. For every beat, provide one distinct complete factual claim, a concrete example, a concise editable visual direction, and one or two exact supplied source IDs. End the claim, example, and visual direction with complete punctuation. Every cited source excerpt must directly support the claim; reuse at least two important technical terms from each cited excerpt so support can be checked locally. Do not invent course assignments, policies, measurements, datasets, instruction encodings, or product behavior that is absent from the supplied excerpts. Keep the claim, example, and visual direction compact; a deterministic local expander will produce the full narration. Sequence the beats from foundations through application and end with a practical analysis checklist. Use only the supplied source excerpts for factual claims. Every factual claim must cite one or more supplied source IDs. Narration must describe information that is essential to understand visuals. Do not imitate a named creator or invent sources.
input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-320: Principles of Data Management. Create a representative course-foundations companion aligned to the official catalog description. It must teach durable concepts and problem-solving methods without claiming to replace the instructor's syllabus. Official catalog description: This course provides a broad introduction to the principles and practice of modern data management, with an emphasis on the relational database model. Topics in relational database systems include data modeling; the relational model; relational algebra; Structured Query Language (SQL); and data quality, transactions, integrity and security. Students will also learn approaches to building relational database application programs. Additional topics include object-oriented and object-relational databases; semi-structured databases (such as XML); and information retrieval. A database project is required. Prerequisites: (MATH-190 or MATH-200) and (CSCI-140 or CSCI-142 or CSCI-242 or SWEN-124 or CSEC-124 or GCIS-124 or GCIS-127) or equivalent courses. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 It may be used to fulfill one of the following: SMTL: Science/Math Literacy Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer Regeneration revision 2: use ten distinct, specific beat titles and avoid repeating any title or section label.

Source excerpts:

[neo4j-graph-data-modeling]
Property graph models represent domain entities as nodes. Relationships connect nodes and have a type and direction. Nodes and relationships can carry properties. Labels group nodes that play a similar domain role. A useful graph model begins from the questions the application must answer. Traversal patterns determine which relationships the application follows. Identity must be explicit when several records may describe the same entity. Constraints and indexes support data integrity and efficient lookup. Direction, cardinality, and update behavior are part of the model.

[postgresql-documentation]
Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types. Primary keys identify rows, while foreign keys express references between tables. Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules. Queries select, join, aggregate, insert, update, and delete data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries. Transactions group operations into an atomic unit of work. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another. Schema design separates entities and relationships, while normalization addresses update anomalies. Query planning and physical structures influence performance without changing logical query meaning.

[rit-csci-320]
This course provides a broad introduction to the principles and practice of modern data management, with an emphasis on the relational database model. Topics in relational database systems include data modeling; the relational model; relational algebra; Structured Query Language (SQL); and data quality, transactions, integrity and security. Students will also learn approaches to building relational database application programs. Additional topics include object-oriented and object-relational databases; semi-structured databases (such as XML); and information retrieval. A database project is required. Prerequisites: (MATH-190 or MATH-200) and (CSCI-140 or CSCI-142 or CSCI-242 or SWEN-124 or CSEC-124 or GCIS-124 or GCIS-127) or equivalent courses. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 It may be used to fulfill one of the following: SMTL: Science/Math Literacy Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

beats.claim: Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types.
beats.example: A 'Students' table contains rows for each student, with columns for ID, name, and major, each with a specific data type like INTEGER or VARCHAR.
beats.title: Foundations of the Relational Model
beats.visualDirection: Display a simple table schema diagram with labeled columns and data types.

beats.claim: Data modeling begins by identifying domain entities and their relationships.
beats.example: Modeling a 'Library' system involves entities like Books, Authors, and Members, connected by relationships like 'writtenBy' and 'checkedOutBy'.
beats.title: Entity-Relationship Modeling Basics
beats.visualDirection: Show a simple ER diagram with three rectangles (Book, Author, Member) and lines connecting them.

beats.claim: Primary keys identify rows and ensure each record is uniquely distinguishable.
beats.example: A 'Products' table uses a 'ProductID' column as the primary key to uniquely identify each item.
beats.title: Primary Keys and Unique Identifiers
beats.visualDirection: Highlight a primary key column in a table diagram with a unique key symbol.

beats.claim: Foreign keys express references between tables and maintain referential integrity.
beats.example: A 'Orders' table includes a 'CustomerID' foreign key that links to the 'Customers' table.
beats.title: Foreign Keys and Referential Integrity
beats.visualDirection: Draw a line from the 'Orders' table to the 'Customers' table labeled 'CustomerID'.

beats.claim: Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules, ensuring data quality.
beats.example: A 'Salary' column constraint prevents negative values, and a 'Email' column constraint enforces a valid email format.
beats.title: Constraints for Data Validation
beats.visualDirection: Show a table with constraint symbols (e.g., NOT NULL, CHECK) next to relevant columns.

beats.claim: Normalization addresses update anomalies by organizing data into logical tables and relationships.
beats.example: Splitting a 'Department' table into separate tables for DepartmentName and DepartmentLocation prevents duplicate data and update errors.
beats.title: Normalization and Update Anomalies
beats.visualDirection: Display a before-and-after table structure showing normalization steps.

beats.claim: Relational algebra provides a mathematical framework for selecting, joining, and aggregating data.
beats.example: A SELECT statement with a JOIN clause combines data from 'Employees' and 'Departments' tables based on a common key.
beats.title: Relational Algebra and Query Logic
beats.visualDirection: Show a simplified relational algebra expression (e.g., σ, ⨝) alongside a corresponding SQL query snippet.

beats.claim: Transactions group operations into an atomic unit of work, ensuring all-or-nothing execution.
beats.example: A banking transaction transfers funds between two accounts; if one step fails, both are rolled back.
beats.title: Transactions and Atomicity
beats.visualDirection: Illustrate a transaction flow with steps (Start, Process, Commit/Rollback) and a lock icon.

beats.claim: Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries, improving performance without changing logical meaning.
beats.example: An index on the 'LastName' column speeds up searches for employees by surname.
beats.title: Indexing and Query Performance
beats.visualDirection: Show a table with a B-tree index structure diagram next to a query execution path.

beats.claim: Students must verify that database designs meet integrity, performance, and query requirements.
beats.example: Check that all foreign keys reference valid primary keys, indexes cover frequent query columns, and constraints prevent invalid data entry.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Display a checklist graphic with three boxes: Integrity, Performance, Query Requirements.

learningObjectives: Define the relational database model and explain how tables, rows, columns, and declared types organize data.
Explain how primary keys, foreign keys, and constraints enforce data integrity and prevent update anomalies.
Demonstrate how normalization and indexing improve database performance and query efficiency.
json.title: CSCI-320: Principles of Data Management
